title: AI Models Can Provably Hide Arbitrary Capabilities
abstract: arXiv:2610.13928v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Capability evaluations aim to surface dangerous model behaviors before deployment, but their reliability depends on the assumption that hidden capabilities can be elicited. We show this assumption does not hold under adversarial conditions by constructing backdoor attacks that embed encrypted neural networks within host model weights, decrypting and executing them only upon receiving a secret trigger. Using digital lockers, these hidden circuits remain provably hard to elicit and interpret under cryptographic assumptions, even given full access to model weights, extending prior work from hiding fixed strings to arbitrary computations. We implement our proof of concept constructions in PyTorch and evaluate elicitation through fine-tuning, weight noising, gradient-based trigger search, and latent adversarial training on a small chemical reaction prediction task - a proxy for CBRN-relevant capabilities. translated_title: AI模型能够可证明地隐藏任意能力
translated_abstract: 能力评估旨在在模型部署前暴露其危险行为，但其可靠性依赖于一个假设：隐藏的能力是可以被引出的。我们通过构建后门攻击证明，这一假设在对抗性条件下并不成立——该攻击将加密的神经网络嵌入宿主模型的权重之中，只有在接收到秘密触发器时才会解密并执行。借助数字保险箱技术，这些隐藏电路在密码学假设下可被证明难以被引出和解释，即使攻击者拥有对模型权重的完全访问权限，这将先前的工作从隐藏固定字符串扩展到了隐藏任意计算。我们在PyTorch中实现了概念验证构建，并在一个小型化学反应预测任务（作为CBRN相关能力的代理任务）上，通过微调、权重加噪、基于梯度的触发器搜索以及潜在对抗训练等方法评估了引出攻击的效果。我们的结果表明，该方法对这些引出手段具有抵抗能力。
tldr: 本文提出一种将加密神经网络嵌入模型权重的后门攻击方法，在密码学假设下可证明地隐藏任意能力，使现有能力评估手段难以引出或解读这些隐藏功能。
en_tdlr: This paper presents backdoor attacks that embed encrypted neural networks within model weights, provably hiding arbitrary capabilities under cryptographic assumptions so that existing capability evaluations fail to elicit or interpret them.
